slideDifferences.nativeText:
To Consider 
1. Adjectives that finish in ING are used to describe situations or things.
2. Adjectives that finish in ED are used to describe how people feel because of something.
3.  Adjectives may be unique or classified into a pattern. E. G: Glib / Silly / Tiny
4. Some ING adjectives are used to describe people if they are producing something in someone else: I am annoyed, you know? Joey is so annoying, always talking too much.
slideDifferences.publishedText: To Consider 1. Adjectives that finish in -ING are normally used to describe situations or things. 2. Adjectives that finish in -ED are used to describe how people feel because of something. 3. Adjectives may be unique or classified into a pattern. E.G.: Glib / Silly / Tiny 4. Some -ING adjectives are used to describe people if they are producing something in someone else: I am annoyed, you know? Joey is so annoying, always talking too much. 5. Another issue is that some adjectives ending -IC and -ICAL tend to be confusing; here is a list for patterns https://www.thefreedictionary.com/Commonly-Confused-Suffixes-ic-vs-ical.htm#:~:text=The%20suffixes%20%E2%80%9C%2Dic%E2%80%9D%20and,are%20notoriously%20difficult%20to%20distinguish. https://www.thefreedictionary.com/Commonly-Confused-Suffixes-ic-vs-ical.htm#:~:text=The%20suffixes%20%E2%80%9C%2Dic%E2%80%9D%20and,are%20notoriously%20difficult%20to%20distinguish

slideDifferences.nativeText:
Although adjectives happen to be in a variety of contexts, their main function is to describe.
Functions
Examples
1
Describe situations or things that affect people.
I have to admit that was a fascinating lesson.
The spa was so relaxing.
2
Describe how people feel by any situation or thing.
The audience is amused.
HAve you heard the story of the crooked man?
To consider 
1. Some adjectives like crooked / naked do not follow the regular pronunciation rule for ED endings. This may be because of the origin of the word or because there is no corresponding verb to the adjective.

slideDifferences.nativeText:
B. Listen to the audio and answer the questions your teacher makes.
Gone to College

It has been such an exciting moment in my life. My name is Diane and I am now a college student. I was always interested in how leaving the house and coming to college would be and I must say it is breathtaking. Of course, I have tons of responsibilities and time-consuming activities but I feel blessed that my parents were able to send me here. Don’t get me wrong, there are some boring lessons and tiring lectures but most of it is amazing. Spending time with my friends and being surrounded by people with similar interests make me feel fortunate and grateful. Are you looking forward to living this experience?
